summary: Poplar Point Light, built at Wickford Harbor in 1831, is the oldest surviving Rhode Island light on its original site. It is now a private house, and it was relit in December 2025.

lens.status: removed (nomination); USLHS lists a 1905 Swedish Fresnel as current optic

corrections.why: No source gives 1765. The nomination and the USLHS record date the tower and dwelling to 1831. The record's 1765 build event should go with it.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's question whether the light is still lit is answered by LighthouseFriends: the Coast Guard gave permission, and the light was relit on Christmas night 2025 as a flashing light. The USLHS record, which predates the relight, lists it as not an active aid.

notes_for_editor: Conflicts left in the story: (1) the builder's cost is $1,888 (nomination) or $1,889 (LighthouseFriends); (2) the dwelling is cut stone and one and a half storeys (nomination) or one-storey rubblestone (LighthouseFriends); (3) the first lens is 1855, sixth order steamer (LighthouseFriends) or 1856 (archive); (4) Henry F. Sherman's stint ends 1882 (archive) or 1885 (LighthouseFriends); (5) Sherman of Pawtucket (nomination) or Pawtuxet (LighthouseFriends); (6) LighthouseFriends prints the plaque's town as Newton, the nomination as Newtown; (7) the archive gives a 1905 Swedish Fresnel as current optic, while the nomination (about 1987) says the lens has been removed; (8) the USLHS record's characteristic 'Fl W 6s' is taken from its 6-second white flash; the light was fixed for most of its life, and LighthouseFriends reports a flashing light from 2025; (9) the record's NRHP listing year (1988) is not checked: NRHP 87001703 suggests a 1987 listing; (10) Edward Andrews (1893-1930) is LighthouseFriends' only; the archive does not list him, and his stint runs past the 1882 discontinuance, as do Nathaniel Dodge's (1885-1893); the sources do not explain this; (11) the relight is reported by LighthouseFriends only in the text read; news search results (WJAR, Independent RI, Narragansett Times) report a Christmas 2025 relight, but those pages were rate-limited and not read, so they are not cited. The private owners are not named; their names appear in the USLHS record and NRHP nomination and are left out. Corpus grep of the Light-House Board volumes for 'Poplar Point' found no entries (Life-Saving Service lists only), so the story rests on the nomination, LighthouseFriends and the USLHS record. No storms or wrecks are sourced for this station, so that chapter is omitted. Roster matched by name and position to USLHS Poplar Point (name match, 1 km or less). A Chronicling America search for Poplar Point (RI, 1880-1900) returned seven pages, all from 1881. The search snippets did not identify a lighthouse item, and reading the pages was rate-limited and did not finish, so no newspaper evidence is used.
